title: Group-wise Reinforcement Feature Generation for Optimal and Explainable Representation Space Reconstruction

problem.claim: Representation space reconstruction is important for addressing dimensionality, generalization, data sparsity, and classic-model availability.

gap.claim: Existing feature engineering and representation learning methods are limited in automation, explainable explicitness, and integration of optimal feature-space reconstruction into downstream tasks.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes a group-wise reinforcement generation perspective for representation space reconstruction.
The paper reformulates representation reconstruction as an interactive process of nested feature generation and selection, generating meaningful explicit features and eliminating redundant ones.
The paper develops cascading reinforcement learning with three cascading Markov Decision Processes and a group-wise generation strategy for feature crossing.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments demonstrating the effectiveness, efficiency, traceability, and explicitness of their system.

narrative_sequence.summary: Representation space supports vectorization, distance computation, pattern characterization, and geometric embedding.
Existing approaches do not fully automate, explain, or optimize representation-space reconstruction for downstream tasks.
The paper frames reconstruction as nested feature generation and selection and applies cascading reinforcement learning to learn generation policies.
A group-wise feature-crossing strategy is introduced, followed by experiments reporting system effectiveness, efficiency, traceability, and explicitness.

source_observation.claim: Existing approaches are described as limited across automation, explainable explicitness, and flexible optimization.

interpretation.claim: A representation-construction method may need to address operational automation, explanation, and task-specific optimization together.

application.claim: Separate feature generation from redundancy-controlling selection and connect both to a task-oriented reinforcement-learning process.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this combination generalizes across tasks or datasets.

unknowns: Datasets, downstream tasks, baselines, metrics, and quantitative results are unspecified.
The abstract does not provide implementation details, computational costs, or reproducibility materials.
